expectations.text: An i18n setup module initializes i18next/react-i18next with en and ja resources
expectations.evidence: The agent created src/i18n.js, which calls i18n.use(initReactI18next).init({...}). Its resources object has en and ja entries built from the imported en/ja checkout.json files.

expectations.text: Translation keys are structured logically in JSON or resource objects, with plural forms for the item count
expectations.evidence: The agent created src/locales/en/checkout.json and src/locales/ja/checkout.json with keys title, total, pay and language. The English file has itemCount_one and itemCount_other. The Japanese file has itemCount_other only, which fits Japanese's single plural category.

expectations.text: Checkout.jsx uses the translation hook instead of hard-coded strings, and the total uses locale-aware currency formatting
expectations.evidence: Checkout.jsx calls useTranslation('checkout') and renders all text through t('title'), t('itemCount', {count}), t('total', {amount}) and t('pay'). The amount comes from new Intl.NumberFormat(i18n.language, {style:'currency', currency:'USD'}).format(total). The currency is fixed to USD, but the formatting follows the locale.

expectations.text: A language switching utility or control is implemented
expectations.evidence: Checkout.jsx has a <select> that lists supportedLanguages and calls i18n.changeLanguage(e.target.value) on change. i18n.js also stores the chosen language in localStorage and updates <html lang> and dir through a languageChanged listener.
